findings.reason: §39 should record the landed reader as the mechanism N3 extends, so the node does not rebuild a reader that exists and its decision is a placement choice against a real algorithm.
findings.text: the plan's §39 treats "closure counts an undisposed sub-floor review row" as unstarted (N3), but sub_floor_dimensions already returns exactly that finding and obligations.py:_sub_floor_items_by_session already turns each into an owed duty with a next_command, landed under c05c04011 — the plan re-proposes machinery it already owns

findings.reason: naming review.py:1815 as the seat to extend collapses an open "where does the rubric live" decision into a one-line signature change, removing N4 as a deliverable.
findings.text: §21's per-role dimension definition and §39's N4 (review-rubric-home) propose where a per-role rubric lives without testing whether declared_dimension_floors, already keyed by dimension name, can take a role dimension, which is the smaller honest change

findings.reason: the plan must name reckon/crew/obligations.py as the owning file and extend its sub-floor duty, or run a second sub-floor count that drifts from the disposition command that retires the first.
findings.text: §39 N3 offers "a new foldable-remaining figure" as a placement for the sub-floor closure count; that duty already exists in obligations.py and reaches the drain through obligation_snapshot.py:804, so a second figure in runs.drain would be a forked count over the same stored review record

findings.reason: resolving N3-N5 against the existing obligation/drain path collapses three decisions into one extension of the mechanism that already carries a dimension duty to the coordinator.
findings.text: the score-reader's remainder is split across three independent decisions (count home, rubric home, owning actor) that all read and score the one stored review record, so the disposition path has no single module and each later change touches three seams

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §39 spreads one capability (a review dimension below its floor must be acted on) across three separate unresolved seams — count home (N3), rubric home (N4), owning actor (N5) — each a fresh decision over the same stored review record, instead of one reader that hides the disposition path behind the interface the plan already has in review.py.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §39 N3's option of "a new foldable-remaining figure" for the sub-floor count duplicates the duty already owned by reckon/crew/obligations.py (_sub_floor_items_by_session) and surfaced through reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:804; the plan must name that owner and extend it rather than fork the reading into runs.drain.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites existing machinery throughout (recovery.py readers, roles.by_spec_level, _generation_rate, the budget records), but §39's N3 poses a "where does the closure count live" decision without citing the already-landed sub-floor duty reader in reckon/crew/review.py:1856 (sub_floor_dimensions) and reckon/crew/obligations.py:707 (_sub_floor_items_by_session), which derive exactly that finding and expose a disposition command.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §21's "the rubric defines each dimension per role" and §39's N4 propose a rubric home without saying why review.py's existing REVIEW_DIMENSIONS tuple (review.py:82) and declared_dimension_floors (review.py:1815) cannot simply take a role key, which would be the extension the item asks for.
